posts.name: Adam
posts.cooked: I think he gets that reputation because he lives in the big city and has a blue-collar line of work (which at this point is really more of a hobby). But he is very old-fashioned in a lot of his ways, and - in no small part thanks to his martial arts training - is far more disciplined in word and deed than your average person. I don’t think he’d consider himself “poor”, as he places little value on material wealth. “Street” is only an apt term for WHERE he is, and his auto shop functions more as a monastery than anything else.

posts.name: lugaru
posts.cooked: Yeah, for me Mr Fixer is one of the more realized, original characters. I could do a little bit of a stretch to compare him to a couple of comics characters but he ultimately is more of something out of “Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance” with a heavy emphasis on “Wax on, Wax off”. Also each one of those stances simultaneously cracks me up and makes me go “awesome!”. Maybe it is because I spent my teens working at my dads hardware store and considered it a personal dojo full of awesome weapons and practical knowledge. I know I attained some level of peace while welding dozens of pipes to shower heads in the alley behind the store.

posts.name: beevolant
posts.cooked:
I think that the characters being a mix of races and genders (and besides Haka) their race/gender not really having anything to do with their powers is one of the things that make the SOTM world so interesting. Not that white men are not interesting, but… well, it’s been done (which is why Legacy is so tongue in cheek campy and awesome). I have already read/seen so many of their stories that when you read/see someone else’s story, it’s just so much fresher.

I think what I really like the most about the SOTM world is that it feels like how comics should be, as opposed to how they are. For two and a half white dudes from the midwest, that is pretty effing sweet.

I also really appreciate female characters who are not all boobs! OMG! I think Adam might be the only male artist drawing women who are not walking T&A shots (also, the women have pretty realistic super hero musculature, I totally dig that too). That’s not only really cool, but also really refreshing. Though, as a metal worker who has breasts and skin, I’ve got to say that I hope Unity wears a shirt more in the shop - unless she likes getting random burns/cuts/scratches or bits of metal polish in her belly button (and from personal experience, neither are fun!). I’m willing to let the safety issues of not having her tied back slide for the aesthetic but the exposed belly goes to far for my suspension of disbelief (see that whole personal experience with polishing grit in the belly button thing, don’t ask questions, I’m allowed to wear whatever I want in the privacy of my own basement and then learn my lesson). Besides the whole sports bra thing is kind of trite and reads 13-year-old-boy fantasy to me.

posts.name: SlenderTroll
posts.cooked: 'Course, it’s probably easier to avoid injury and metal-polish-navel when you don’t actually touch the stuff you’re working with.

posts.name: Adam
posts.cooked: I’d meant it as functional, and she does have a hoodie also, it’s just tied around her waist for now. Slender Troll’s pretty dead-on as far as what I was thinking with wardrobe - her priority’s going to be comfort as she doesn’t actually have to weld or forge anything by hand, and shop safety’s not really an issue for her. Safety from villain attacks is another matter entirely.
